Hey, I'm working on a gritty crime noir script set in a big city. I want to make the neighborhood feel real and lived-in, not like some sanitized movie version. Can you help me come up with a few character sketches for some of the low-level guys running things on the street level? Like the guys you'd see hanging out on corners or working the small-time hustles in the rougher parts of town. Just looking for that authentic, tough atmosphere.

Absolutely, I can help with that. Here are some character sketches to bring the gritty atmosphere of a rough city neighborhood to life.

1. **Vince "The Viper" Corleone** – Tiny, wiry, with a jagged smile always brimming behind the front teeth, Vince works as a numbers guy, running small-time hustles for more gruff and vengeful characters. He's seen gutting cars, dealing with crooked small businesses, and always has a new scam ready to take off. His greasy hair only adds to his unkempt appearance, and his eyes gleam with calculating resilience. He's a known loner, someone grappling with quieter moments where he cherishes the fleeting solace in the dimly lit bars of The Garden Floor.

2. **Sergeant Jake "Beard" Callahan** – Tough-looking, Jake got his scruff from years in the city's back alleys doing small-time hustles before he nicked up to the beat. He's lazy except when the cash stacks up, and he's quick to rely on the muscle if trouble brews. Humble and smiling promises, Jake's eyes scan for the next target, someone who needs using or selling.
